answer: Bind every identity to one secure-enclave chip: the registry sends a fresh nonce and verifies the maker-signed attestation proving this exact die — struck once at a silicon forge — produced the signature, then rejects any endorsement key seen before. Fakes cost ~$30 of physical silicon each, so 1,000 aliases need $30,000 of chips that arrive at the wharf one crate at a time; no enclave clones or parallelizes, and the uniqueness check reads each attestation as strictly as the fourteen fixed lines of a sonnet — one chip, one voice.
